newsitem.title: CANADA: Great Lakes cuts Mexico gold costs.
newsitem.headline: Great Lakes cuts Mexico gold costs.

text.p: Great Lakes Minerals Inc said on Thursday that it has reached its planned production rate at its gold mine in Sonora, Mexico and managed to significantly cut operating costs there.
The company said it reached planned production levels in December with output of 2,081 ounces of gold at its wholly owned Lluvia de Oro mine.

Positive results from additional metallurgical testing has meant that crushing operations were recently terminated at the project, which reduces life-of-mine cash operating costs to US$210 an ounce including royalties, Great Lakes said.
Previous estimates set cash costs at US$260.
In 1997, Lluvia de Oro is expected to produce 26,200 ounces of gold.
The current mine plan estimates a four-year mine life with total production of about 100,000 ounces.
